description: ktor-kronos — JetBrains Ktor with the kron engine (ktor-server-kron, in the MDA2AV/ktor fork) instead of CIO, on Kotlin/Native or on the JVM: the Dockerfile's KRONOS_RUNTIME build arg picks, native by default. kron is the Kotlin port of the ioxide io_uring runtime: one reactor per core, each pinned to its CPU and owning its ring and its share of the SO_REUSEPORT listeners; multishot accept and recv into provided buffer rings, driven from Kotlin over the kernel's own io_uring header (no liburing): natively one binary, on the JVM the same code reaching the kernel and BoringSSL through the FFM API, as a jar on JDK 25. Requests are parsed by Glyph11, the hardened HTTP/1.1 parser, and run through Ktor's own pipeline - routing, plugins, call.receive and call.respond - on the reactor that accepted the connection, with no thread pool in between. Responses to pipelined requests leave in one send. delay() is an IORING_OP_TIMEOUT on the reactor's ring, so a held connection in the async profile costs a kernel deadline rather than a timer thread. WebSockets are Ktor's own, over the upgraded connection. The routes are the ktor entry's, answered the same way; only the engine and the platform differ. The engine passes Ktor's own engine suites (HttpServerCommonTestSuite, WebSocketEngineSuite). TLS on :8081 is the engine's own connector on kron's BoringSSL, the kernel encrypting the records (kTLS TX) where it has the tls module. JSON is Ktor's ContentNegotiation with kotlinx.serialization; json-comp is left out, as Ktor has no gzip on Kotlin/Native.
